title: Four students killed, 32 hurt as truck rams parked school bus on Lucknow-Agra Expressway
dek: The bus, carrying 50 people back from a school trip to the Taj Mahal, had stopped on the shoulder near Kannauj before dawn.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Four schoolchildren were killed and 32 people injured when a truck crashed into the back of a parked school bus on the Lucknow-Agra Expressway near Thathia in Uttar Pradesh's Kannauj district at about 6 am on Tuesday, police said.

The bus, belonging to a private school in Kaushambi district, was carrying 50 people, most of them students, back from an excursion to the Taj Mahal in Agra. It had pulled onto the shoulder so the children could use the toilet when the truck, which reports said was speeding, hit it from behind, crushing its rear.

Police, staff of the Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority and passing motorists pulled the children out. The injured "were subsequently taken to a medical college in ambulances, where doctors declared four of them dead," Superintendent of Police Vinod Kumar said. The dead were aged 14 to 17. The injured include 24 students and eight school staff, according to reports; reports differ slightly on the number of children hurt. One critically injured child and the school's manager were referred to Kanpur for treatment.

District Magistrate Ashutosh Mohan Agnihotri and the SP visited the injured at the medical college. Uninjured students were sent home on another bus. Police had not said by Tuesday afternoon whether the truck driver had been held, and no compensation had been announced.
